title: SpectraFit-Core-Reproducibility: every published result of spectrafit-core 0.1.3, regenerated from the release
description:
A pinned, thin consumer of the spectrafit-core release that regenerates the NIST StRD agreement tables, the figures and the timing comparison reported in the article on spectrafit-core, on a recorded host (terra, Linux x86-64), and checks every number stated in the text against the regenerated data. The compiled library is the published PyPI wheel; the harness and the figure scripts come from the release tag.

Version 1.3.0 moves the archive to spectrafit-core 0.1.3: the published PyPI wheel, and the harness, figure scripts and example gallery of tag v0.1.3. The timing benchmark of record is re-measured on terra on 16 and 17 November 2026 with the 0.1.3 wheel at the same repetition depths and seeds; the two measurements with 0.1.2 are kept next to it. It adds the speed-up at a common stopping tolerance, the analytic against finite-difference Jacobian, both NIST certified starts, a stationarity audit, 500 far starts of the Fe L2,3 fit, the example gallery, the quick start and an overview report, and as supplementary material the Fe L2,3 fit from 500 seeded starts with and without the four tied relationships. The claims are recomputed for 0.1.3; the changed checks and the known failures of the default case catalogue are listed in the README.

Version 1.3.1 keeps the pin to spectrafit-core 0.1.3. It adds the target interop-fe-l23, the Fe L2,3 constrained model as one graph JSON file fitted by SpectraFit-Core and by lmfit through the release's translator, with four claims; the example folder now holds the Python files of the gallery with a generated index; the known failures are described in more detail; and the README is reordered.

Version 1.3.2 keeps the pin to spectrafit-core 0.1.3. It adds the target nist-params, which stores the fitted parameter values of SpectraFit-Core and lmfit on the 22 NIST StRD problems next to the certified values and standard deviations, guarded against the worst log relative errors of Table 1 cell for cell, with one claim without a threshold; and the target bias-batches, which repeats the serialisation-bias measurement of the release and keeps every timed batch of both sides.
